method: Three fresh sessions per build, zero warm spares, four streamed turns each: first web search, warm web search, Python tool and managed-history recall. Candidate sessions then baseline sessions; last candidate cleanup overlaps control startup. Same model, prompts and shared dependency versions. Each source differs from its previously tested project only in agent.toml, adding app-auth system.ai.web_search. MCP is discovered during graph construction per invocation. Provider VM/cache and search/model latency uncontrolled. Small samples, no latency-percentile claims.

baseline.manifest:
schema_version = 1

[agent]
framework = "langgraph"
server = "agentbricks"
deployment_name = "sb-lean-1114"

[session_store]
name = "sb-lean-1114-sessions"

[memory_store]
name = "sb-lean-1114-memory"

[tracing]
experiment_name = "/Shared/agentbricks_traces/sb-lean-1114"
[[tools]]
id = "web_search"
auth = "app"
source = {kind = "mcp", service = "system.ai.web_search"}

validation.unit_tests: No SDK/runtime code changed; benchmark lint/format and live API/SSE checks executed. Prior unit evidence remains in the five-second report.
validation.ui: No UI source changes. API configs expose web_search. No new browser recording.

cleanup: All six session stop responses confirmed stopped; see per-sample timing records. Both Apps remain running with zero warm spares.
limitations: MCP discovery is outside handler preparation and runs on every graph build.
Graph-build timing combines imports, discovery and construction; it is not a discovery-only measurement.
The model may issue multiple searches; every call remains in the evidence.
Provider warmth/search/model latency uncontrolled; three sessions do not establish a percentile.
Existing dependency compatibility plan, optional integrations, live OpenAI and custom servers remain outside this measurement.
